picks.intervention_label: Lirafugratinib (RLY-4008)
picks.rationale: If the pending CGP returns an FGFR2 fusion, this is the biggest upside on the board: ORR 46.5% (95% CI 37.1-56.1), DCR 96.5%, mPFS 11.3 mo in the FGFRi-naive ReFocus cohort of 114, and the FGFR2-selective design largely dodges the FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia that dogs pemigatinib. I know the weakness and I am naming it: the evidence is an ASCO GI 2026 abstract with no PMID, the drug is pre-approval (PDUFA Sept 2026), and everything rides on a fusion nobody has tested yet. In a treatment-naive-to-FGFR patient with ~10-15% pretest odds of the axis being live, that is a bet I take, because the response and durability numbers beat the on-label agents. Access before approval means a trial slot or expanded access, so line that up in parallel with the genomic panel.
primary_concerns: Whole thing is dead on arrival if FGFR2 fusion is negative on CGP
Abstract-only data, no peer-reviewed full text and no PMID; grade 3+ PPE 32.8% is a real quality-of-life hit
Not yet FDA-approved, so real-world access depends on a trial or expanded-access route

picks.intervention_label: Futibatinib
picks.rationale: The FGFR2 play I would actually reach for first if I want published, on-label evidence rather than an abstract: FOENIX-CCA2 gave ORR 42% (95% CI 32-52), mDoR 9.7 mo, mOS 21.7 mo in NEJM, with only 2% discontinuing for toxicity. Its covalent irreversible chemistry holds up against several FGFR2 kinase-domain resistance mutations that sink the reversible inhibitors, so it doubles as a sequencing option after pemigatinib. Same hard gate as every FGFR pick here: the fusion is untested. I rank it just under lirafugratinib only because the raw response and PFS numbers are a notch lower, not because the evidence is weaker; the evidence is stronger.
primary_concerns: Requires a confirmed FGFR2 fusion the patient has not been tested for
Hyperphosphatemia grade 3+ in 30%, higher than the selective next-gen agents
Intrahepatic subsite drove the trial; the patient's subsite is unspecified at intake

picks.intervention_label: Larotrectinib
picks.rationale: This is the highest response rate anywhere in the dossier: ORR 79% (95% CI 72-85), mDoR 35.2 mo, mOS 44.4 mo, with grade 3 AEs in just 13%. NTRK fusions run under 1% in CCA, so the pretest probability is grim, but the flip side is that when it hits, the response is close to automatic and lasts years, and the toxicity is the gentlest of any targeted option here. The RNA arm of the rank-1 paired panel catches the fusion at almost no extra cost, so the downside of looking is basically zero. I would rather chase a 1% shot at a 79%-ORR, 44-month-OS drug than not look.
primary_concerns: NTRK fusion prevalence <1% in CCA; most likely a dry well
DNA-only NGS can miss the fusion, so RNA-based calling has to be in the ordered panel
No CCA-specific efficacy; benefit rests on the tumor-agnostic fusion mechanism

picks.intervention_label: Gunagratinib (ICP-192)
picks.rationale: The eye-catching FGFR2 number is here: ORR 52.9% (9/17 PR), DCR 94.1% in the ICP-CL-00301 expansion, higher than any approved FGFR agent. I am not fooling myself about the n of 17 or the abstract-only, ROBINS-I Serious status, so I keep it as a fourth-line FGFR shot rather than the anchor. It earns a slot because a covalent pan-FGFR inhibitor with orphan designation and a recruiting phase 2 (NCT05678270) gives an FGFR2-positive patient another door, especially for sequencing. Same fusion gate applies, and the confidence interval on that 52.9% is wide enough to drive a truck through.
primary_concerns: n=17, no confidence interval reported; the point estimate could move a lot with more patients
Abstract-only, ROBINS-I Serious, and investigational with US access likely trial-only
Dead if FGFR2 fusion is negative

picks.intervention_label: Dabrafenib + trametinib
picks.rationale: A confirmed BRAF V600E opens a 47% ORR (95% CI 31-62) with mPFS 9.0 mo from the ROAR biliary cohort, plus a tumor-agnostic label, so a positive call is immediately actionable off the same CGP. BRAF V600E sits at only 1-5% of biliary cancer, but the response rate rivals the FGFR agents and the doublet is well-characterized with pyrexia as the main nuisance rather than an organ threat. I rank it here rather than higher because the prevalence is low and the pick lives or dies on the NGS result. If it comes back positive, I would not hesitate.
primary_concerns: BRAF V600E prevalence 1-5%; likely negative
Non-V600E class 2/3 BRAF alterations do not qualify and could be miscalled as actionable
Pyrexia in ~19% needs active management though it is rarely dangerous

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib
picks.rationale: The one randomized phase 3 signal in the whole set: ClarIDHy gave a PFS HR of 0.37 (95% CI 0.25-0.54, p<0.0001) versus placebo with a low risk-of-bias grade, and IDH1 R132 shows up in 15-20% of intrahepatic CCA, so the pretest odds are respectable. My honest hesitation is the effect size, not the evidence quality: ORR was 2%, median PFS 2.7 mo, and the OS read got blunted by crossover to a crossover-adjusted HR 0.46. For a persona that weights magnitude, a hazard ratio this clean but an absolute benefit this thin lands it at the bottom of my ranked picks rather than off the list.
primary_concerns: Absolute PFS gain is small (2.7 vs 1.4 mo) despite the strong HR
ORR only 2%; disease stabilization rather than tumor shrinkage is the realistic goal
Gated on a confirmed IDH1 R132 mutation, untested here

notes: Scope-unknown CCA with every axis ngs_pending, so the rank-1 shared move is the comprehensive genomic profiling itself; my six picks are all conditional on which axis the paired DNA+RNA panel lights up. I leaned the ranking toward the FGFR2-selective next-gen agents (lirafugratinib, gunagratinib) over the approved incumbents because the response and durability numbers are higher, even though the data are abstract-only and pre-approval; that is the risktaker trade of magnitude for evidence maturity, made explicit. Deliberately left off HER2 T-DXd despite the 61.3% IHC 3+ subgroup ORR because the ILD signal (10.5%, three treatment-related deaths in DESTINY-PanTumor02) sits closest to a safety line, and with zero organ-function labs supplied I will not champion it blind; zanidatamab is the cleaner HER2 bet if that axis confirms. Order CGP with an RNA fusion arm and HER2 IHC/ISH up front so no live axis gets missed.

picks.intervention_label: Comprehensive genomic profiling (paired DNA + RNA NGS, plus HER2 IHC/ISH and MMR IHC) before any targeted therapy
picks.rationale: Nothing here carries less risk than the test itself. A paired DNA/RNA panel has no toxicity, and it resolves seven of the eight candidate axes in one pass, so every drug below is gated on it. There is a roughly 40% chance of finding something actionable, and starting a targeted agent on an unconfirmed marker is exactly the harm I want to avoid. Add the HER2 IHC with reflex ISH and the MMR IHC as parallel orders, since NGS copy number alone does not tell you which anti-HER2 agent applies and a low-purity sample can miss an MSI call. NCCN advises CGP at diagnosis of unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer. This is the one recommendation I hold at high confidence.
primary_concerns: RNA-based fusion calling matters: DNA-only panels miss a subset of FGFR2 fusions with novel or intronic breakpoints, so confirm the ordered assay includes an RNA arm.
Every therapeutic pick below is conditional on this returning a positive, confirmed call; a clean negative sends the patient to standard chemotherapy, not to any drug on this list.
Archival block quality and tumor purity can degrade the read; a ctDNA parallel is the faster fallback when tissue is limited, at some cost to fusion sensitivity.

picks.intervention_label: Pemigatinib (only if an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement is confirmed)
picks.rationale: Of the FGFR options this is the one with the longest track record: FDA approval since 2020, so roughly five years of post-marketing safety follow-up on top of the FIGHT-202 pivotal. The toxicity is on-target and predictable. Hyperphosphatemia ran 55% any grade with no grade 3-4 in the trial, and it has a well-worn management algorithm of low-phosphate diet, phosphate binders, and dose holds. The nail, skin, and dysgeusia effects are mostly low grade, and serous retinal detachment at 4% has an established ophthalmologic monitoring pathway. Grade 3+ AEs sat at 64% in the 146-patient safety population, which I do not minimize, but the events are ones oncologists already know how to run. ORR was 35.5% (95% CI 26.5-45.4). FGFR2 fusion is also the highest-yield axis at roughly 10-15% in intrahepatic disease, so this is the confirmed-positive I most expect to see.
primary_concerns: Fusion is untested (ngs_pending) and subsite is unspecified; eligibility was built on intrahepatic CCA, so a non-intrahepatic subsite weakens the match.
Serous retinal detachment (4%, one grade 3) requires baseline and periodic ophthalmologic exams before and during treatment.
Single-arm phase 2 pivotal; the efficacy read has no randomized comparator even though the safety base is now mature.

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib (only if an IDH1 R132 mutation is confirmed)
picks.rationale: This is the cleanest safety dataset in the whole dossier, and that is why I rank it here despite a modest efficacy signal. ClarIDHy is the only randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 on the board (RoB2 low), and the grade 3+ AE profile tracked placebo closely: ascites was the most common grade 3+ event in both arms at 7%, and there were no treatment-related deaths. The one class effect to watch is QT prolongation, which showed up as a single grade 3 event and has a standard ECG-monitoring answer. Yes, the median PFS gain is only 2.7 versus 1.4 months and the ORR is 2%, with the OS read blunted by 70% crossover (HR 0.37 for PFS, p<0.0001; crossover-adjusted OS HR 0.46). But for a patient where do-no-harm is the priority, a well-tolerated oral agent with randomized evidence and a benign toxicity ledger is a defensible confirmed-positive choice. IDH1 mutations run roughly 15-20% in intrahepatic disease.
primary_concerns: Absolute PFS benefit is small and the ORR is 2%; this buys disease control and tolerability, not deep responses.
IDH1 R132 is untested; IDH2 and non-R132 IDH1 variants do not qualify, so the DNA panel must cover the exact hotspot.
QT prolongation is a known class effect and warrants baseline and on-treatment ECGs.

picks.intervention_label: Larotrectinib (only if an NTRK1/2/3 fusion is confirmed)
picks.rationale: If the RNA panel returns an NTRK fusion, this is the best-tolerated targeted agent on the board, which is what earns it a spot for me even at sub-1% prevalence. Across a 260-patient pooled safety population, grade 3 AEs were 13% and grade 4 under 1%, with the worst offenders (ALT rise 3%, anemia 2%, neutropenia 2%) all low single digits and no treatment-related deaths. The selectivity for TRK spares much of the off-target load that broader inhibitors carry. The efficacy is a bonus rather than my rationale here: ORR 79% (95% CI 72-85), median DoR 35.2 months. I would still counsel that the prior probability of a positive test is very low in CCA, so this is a low-confidence pick driven by how favorable the safety and durability are if the fusion is actually there.
primary_concerns: Sub-1% prevalence in CCA; a negative read, which is the likely outcome, drops this to zero.
Evidence is single-arm and pooled across tumor types with no biliary-specific cohort and no randomized comparator.
CNS-related low-grade effects (dizziness, weight gain) occur and warrant counseling, though they rarely reach grade 3.

picks.intervention_label: Zanidatamab (only if HER2 is confirmed by IHC 2+/3+ with reflex ISH)
picks.rationale: For the HER2 axis I put the antibody ahead of the ADC on safety grounds. Zanidatamab's toxicity is manageable and mostly familiar: diarrhea 40% any grade with 5% grade 3, infusion-related reactions 35%, and a HER2-class decreased-ejection-fraction signal at 3% grade 3 that inherits the cardiac-monitoring algorithm built over decades of trastuzumab use. HERIZON-BTC-01 gave a confirmed ORR of 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8) with a median DoR of 12.9 months. I deliberately rank this over trastuzumab deruxtecan, whose 10.5% adjudicated interstitial lung disease rate and three treatment-related ILD deaths in DESTINY-PanTumor02 are the kind of uncharacterized long-tail toxicity I flag, even with no toxicity veto set in preferences. The gate is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH, not an NGS amplification call, and HER2 skews toward extrahepatic and gallbladder disease, so subsite uncertainty is the main soft spot.
primary_concerns: HER2 status is untested and the correct gate is IHC with reflex ISH, not an NGS-only amplification signal.
Decreased ejection fraction (3% grade 3) requires baseline and periodic cardiac function monitoring.
HER2 is more common in extrahepatic/gallbladder disease, and subsite is unspecified at intake, weakening the prior.

notes: Re-run over the full current option set (16 new on-axis trials plus new clinical evidence added by the 2026-07 screener/clinician passes). Conservative framing: rank-1 is the non-toxic CGP gate; therapeutic picks 2-5 are each conditional on a confirmed positive and ordered by depth of safety follow-up and predictability of the AE profile, not by peak effect size. Deliberate omissions and their missing safety data, for the round-2 record: (1) Futibatinib is a reasonable FGFR2 alternative but its grade 3 hyperphosphatemia rate is 30% versus pemigatinib's 0% grade 3-4, so I default to the longer-approved, lower-grade option unless a pemigatinib-resistance kinase-domain mutation is documented, which would then justify the switch. (2) Trastuzumab deruxtecan is held below zanidatamab specifically on the 10.5% adjudicated ILD / three ILD deaths signal; this is the pick I would most likely issue a round-2 toxicity qualifier or veto against if it is ranked first by another persona without an ILD-mitigation plan (baseline and serial CT, pneumonitis algorithm, patient-reported dyspnea monitoring). (3) The next-gen selective FGFR2 agents (lirafugratinib ORR 46.5%, tinengotinib, TYRA-200, gunagratinib, fanregratinib) are mechanistically attractive for sparing FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia, but lirafugratinib carries 32.8% grade 3+ palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia and the rest are phase 1/2 or abstract-only with no mature safety follow-up and, for several, no US access; the specific missing datum is durable long-tail tolerability at registration scale, so I do not rank a novel FGFR2-selective agent above the approved pemigatinib. (4) Dabrafenib+trametinib (BRAF V600E) and pembrolizumab (MSI-H/TMB-high) are legitimate confirmed-positive options I did not rank into the top five; pyrexia management for the BRAF doublet and immune-mediated AE algorithms for pembrolizumab are both well-characterized, so my omission is prevalence-and-crowding, not a safety objection. All picks assume ECOG 1 and no prior lines as stated in the assumption set; if real molecular results, prior therapy, organ function, or preferences arrive, re-run intake and this ranking narrows to whichever axis tests positive.

picks.intervention_label: Comprehensive genomic profiling (paired DNA + RNA NGS with fusion calling, MSI, TMB) + HER2 IHC/ISH and MMR IHC
picks.rationale: Read the profile before ranking any drug: all eight candidate axes are ngs_pending, so every therapeutic row below is a hypothesis with no measurement behind it. Ranking a targeted agent above the confirmatory test inverts the actual decision order. A single paired DNA+RNA panel resolves seven of the eight features at once, and the RNA arm matters because DNA-only calling misses a chunk of FGFR2 fusions with intronic or novel breakpoints. Roughly a 40% chance of hitting an actionable alteration sits behind this one test. I put it at rank 1 not as a formality but because nothing else in the dossier is actionable until it returns, and the ORR figures people are about to quote are all conditional on a result we do not have.
primary_concerns: Not a therapy, so it carries no RoB/ROBINS-I profile of its own; the risk is procedural, that the board treats an untested biomarker as if it were confirmed.
DNA-only panels miss a subset of FGFR2 fusions; confirm the ordered panel includes RNA-based fusion calling or the FGFR2 axis can read falsely negative.
HER2 and dMMR need protein/ISH readouts (IHC 4B5, MMR IHC), not an NGS copy-number or MSI score alone, so a single DNA panel does not close those two axes.

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib (conditional on confirmed IDH1 R132)
picks.rationale: This is the only intervention in the whole option set backed by a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3. ClarIDHy is RoB2:Low and hit its registered PFS primary endpoint (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.25-0.54, p<0.0001). On evidence quality alone it clears everything else here, which is all single-arm. I want to be precise about what it buys, though: ORR was 2%, so the benefit is delayed progression rather than tumor shrinkage, and the survival story is unresolved. The intention-to-treat OS HR was 0.69 (p=0.060) and did not cross alpha; the 0.46 that gets cited is an RPSFT crossover adjustment after 70% of placebo patients crossed over, which is a sensitivity model, not the trial result. Rank 2 because it is gated on an IDH1 R132 call we have not made.
primary_concerns: ITT OS was not significant at the pre-specified alpha (HR 0.69, p=0.060); the 0.46 crossover-adjusted figure is modeling, not a clean survival endpoint.
IDH1 R132 is untested (ngs_pending); the entire pick collapses if the hotspot is wild-type, and a limited fusion-only panel could miss the codon.
RoB2: PFS in a symptomatic disease is the residual domain, mitigated but not erased by independent review.

picks.intervention_label: Futibatinib (conditional on confirmed FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement)
picks.rationale: The FGFR2-fusion axis is the closest thing to replication in this dossier, and that is what earns it rank 3 rather than any single ORR. FOENIX-CCA2 (ORR 42%, 95% CI 32-52, median OS 21.7 mo, 2% discontinuing for toxicity) and FIGHT-202 converge on the same effect direction in centrally confirmed fusions, and the new FGFR2-selective agents point the same way. The hard ceiling is that the registered endpoint is ORR, a surrogate, with no randomized comparator and no OS control. I put futibatinib at the head of the FGFR lane because its activity against some post-pemigatinib kinase-domain resistance mutations is documented in the trial rather than extrapolated, which is a sequencing fact I can stand on.
primary_concerns: Single-arm design with a surrogate ORR primary endpoint; no comparator, so the response rate carries the usual single-arm inflation.
FGFR2 fusion is untested (ngs_pending) and eligibility was built on intrahepatic CCA while subsite is unspecified at intake.
Open-label response ascertainment; independent central review reduces the bias but does not remove it.

picks.intervention_label: Lirafugratinib (RLY-4008; conditional on confirmed FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement)
picks.rationale: The FGFR2-selective class is the most interesting new signal in this refresh, and I want to name both its strength and its two weak points. ReFocus reported ORR 46.5% (95% CI 37.1-56.1) in n=114 FGFRi-naive CCA with an FGFR2-selective design that largely spares FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia, which is a real tolerability argument. But this is abstract-only (ASCO GI 2026, no PubMed record, ROBINS-I:Moderate on an unread full paper), and it is single-arm ORR like the rest of the class, so I discount it below the two approved FGFR agents that have peer-reviewed pivotal data. One point that keeps getting garbled: lirafugratinib's own basket NCT07359820 EXCLUDES cholangiocarcinoma, so nobody should cite that trial as an enrollment route here. The 46.5% comes from the separate ReFocus CCA cohort, not the basket. NDA is under FDA priority review with a Sept 2026 PDUFA, so its status is still pending.
primary_concerns: Abstract-only readout; the full paper is unread, so I cannot verify the RoB profile beyond the ROBINS-I:Moderate placeholder and cannot audit response ascertainment or censoring.
Single-arm ORR with no comparator; not yet approved (PDUFA pending), so this is investigational, not an on-label option.
The often-cited basket NCT07359820 does not enroll CCA; conflating it with the ReFocus cohort is an evidence-provenance error to flag, and FGFR2 status is untested here regardless.

picks.intervention_label: Zanidatamab (conditional on confirmed HER2 IHC 2+/3+ with ISH amplification)
picks.rationale: HER2 is the other on-indication axis with a pivotal single-arm readout rather than a basket subgroup. HERIZON-BTC-01 cohort 1 reported confirmed ORR 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8, n=80) with median DoR 12.9 mo, ROBINS-I:Moderate, driving accelerated approval. I rank it fifth, below the FGFR lane, for two reasons: it is single-arm ORR with no comparator, and the gating test is HER2 IHC 4B5 with reflex ISH, not the NGS panel, so a copy-number amplification call alone will not qualify the patient or pick the right agent. I am deliberately keeping the HER2 early-phase crowd (T-DXd basket subgroup, the bispecifics, ADCs, CAR-NK, neratinib) off my ranked list: those are basket subgroup signals or phase-1 dose-finding with no CCA efficacy readout, and I will not rank a subgroup or a first-in-human safety run ahead of a pivotal cohort.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 2b, confirmed-ORR endpoint, accelerated approval; no randomized survival comparison exists.
Gating test is HER2 IHC/ISH (4B5), not the DNA panel; an NGS amplification signal alone does not establish protein expression or select the agent, and HER2 is untested here.
Cardiac signal (decreased ejection fraction) warrants monitoring; more relevant to extrahepatic/gallbladder subsite, which is unspecified at intake.

notes: Re-run over the refreshed option set (16 new on-axis trials, 6 new clinical-evidence rows). My ranking barely moves on structure because the evidence hierarchy did not: one RCT (ClarIDHy, RoB2:Low), a replicated single-arm FGFR2 lane, and a pivotal single-arm HER2 cohort, all sitting behind an unmeasured molecular profile. The new material is mostly abstract-only or conference-reported next-generation agents (lirafugratinib ReFocus, gunagratinib n=17, fanregratinib no indexed identifier, tinengotinib ph1 n=11 FGFR2 subset, zurletrectinib adult ORR sponsor-reported): mechanistically coherent, but I discount abstract-only and sponsor-reported data appropriately and none of it displaces the peer-reviewed pivotals. I did NOT rank: the FGFR2 next-gen agents below lirafugratinib (gunagratinib n=17 is underpowered; fanregratinib is a China-registration abstract with no per-term safety and US access unclear; tinengotinib rank rests on an 11-patient ph1 subset, ROBINS-I:Serious); the pembrolizumab MSI-H and TMB-high rows (no CCA-specific subgroup ORR published, ~1-3% prevalence, decision-changing only if positive); dabrafenib+trametinib (ROAR basket cohort, n=43, ORR by investigator, ~1-5% prevalence); the NTRK/RET agents (<1% prevalence, pooled single-arm baskets); adagrasib (KRYSTAL-1 biliary n=12, ROBINS-I:Serious). These are all legitimate conditional options if their biomarker tests positive, but I will not rank an underpowered subgroup or a phase-1 dose-finding run ahead of a pivotal cohort or an RCT. Provenance flag carried forward: NCT07359820 (lirafugratinib basket) EXCLUDES CCA; the ReFocus cohort is the on-axis data, and the two should not be conflated. Full-paper RoB profiles for the abstract-only rows (lirafugratinib, gunagratinib, fanregratinib) are unread; my discount reflects that, not a claim to have adjudicated them.

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib (if IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor NGS)
picks.rationale: If the IDH1 hotspot reads positive, ivosidenib is the strongest guideline anchor in this whole option set: NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 now lists it category 1 for subsequent-line IDH1-mutant disease, and the 2024 ESMO interim BTC update recommends it after at least one prior line (ESMO-MCBS v1.1 score 2). It is also the only randomized phase 3 among the candidate axes, ClarIDHy, with a PFS HR of 0.37 (95% CI 0.25-0.54). I rank it first on that category-1 status, not on shrinkage, since ORR was only 2% and the realistic aim is delayed progression. IDH1 R132 runs 15-20% in intrahepatic CCA, so it is also one of the likelier positives the panel returns.
primary_concerns: IDH1 R132 is untested (ngs_pending); a negative NGS read voids the pick.

The category-1 listing sits on a phase 3 whose ITT overall survival did not separate (HR 0.69, p=0.060); the 0.46 is RPSFT crossover-adjusted modeling. NCCN graded it category 1 on the PFS win with crossover-adjusted OS support, which is worth naming rather than glossing.
Guidelines assume measurable progression and an ECOG-fit patient; intake gave no organ-function labs and ECOG 1 is an assumption, so QT-monitoring feasibility is unconfirmed.

picks.intervention_label: Futibatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: On a confirmed FGFR2 fusion, futibatinib is NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A for subsequent-line disease, and the 2024 ESMO interim update backs the FGFR-inhibitor class after one prior line at ESMO-MCBS v1.1 score 3. FOENIX-CCA2 gave ORR 42% (95% CI 32-52), median OS 21.7 months, and only 2% stopped for toxicity. I edge it ahead of pemigatinib because it holds activity against some FGFR2 kinase-domain mutations that defeat the reversible inhibitors, which matters for sequencing. FGFR2 fusions sit at 10-15% in intrahepatic CCA, the highest-yield molecular axis to test in this disease.
primary_concerns: FGFR2 fusion is untested (ngs_pending); the indication was built in intrahepatic CCA and subsite is blank at intake, so a non-intrahepatic primary weakens the fit.

Category 2A here reflects single-arm phase 2 with a surrogate ORR endpoint, not a randomized survival comparison. The MCBS 3 is scored on the FGFR-inhibitor class, not on futibatinib over pemigatinib.
On-target hyperphosphatemia hits grade 3 in 30% and needs the phosphate management the guideline assumes is on hand.

picks.intervention_label: Pemigatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: Pemigatinib is the other guideline-endorsed FGFR2 option, NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A and ESMO-recommended within the same FGFR-inhibitor class (MCBS v1.1 score 3), and it was the first FGFR inhibitor approved in CCA with a companion diagnostic behind it. FIGHT-202 gave ORR 35.5% (95% CI 26.5-45.4). I place it just below futibatinib because the sequencing edge on kinase-domain resistance runs the other way, so once the fusion is confirmed this is a within-lane call. Two independent single-arm trials converging on the same fusion axis is what gives the consensus its footing here.
primary_concerns: FGFR2 fusion is untested (ngs_pending); subsite unspecified at intake against an intrahepatic-built indication.
Single-arm phase 2 behind an accelerated approval; the reported OS of 21.1 months is immature at 40 events.
Serous retinal detachment (4%) needs the scheduled ophthalmologic monitoring the guideline presumes, unconfirmed here.

picks.intervention_label: Zanidatamab (if HER2 IHC 3+ with reflex ISH confirmed)
picks.rationale: Zanidatamab is the guideline-endorsed HER2 lead here: NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A for HER2-positive (IHC 3+) subsequent-line disease off HERIZON-BTC-01 (confirmed ORR 41.3%, 95% CI 30.4-52.8, median DoR 12.9 months). It is the only dedicated biliary HER2 trial behind a guideline listing, which is why I rank it over T-DXd (basket route) and over the wave of investigational HER2 agents now on the trial list, none of which any society endorses. The gate is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH on the trial's own scoring, not a breast or gastric cutoff and not an NGS copy-number call standing in for the protein read. HER2 skews toward extrahepatic and gallbladder disease, so a positive depends on a subsite intake never gave.
primary_concerns: HER2 is untested and needs IHC plus reflex ISH, not NGS amplification alone, to meet the guideline gate.
The category 2A rests on single-arm phase 2b accelerated-approval data with no randomized comparator.
HER2 prevalence hinges on a subsite intake left blank, and no baseline cardiac function was supplied for the 3% grade-3 ejection-fraction signal.

picks.intervention_label: Dabrafenib + trametinib (if BRAF V600E confirmed on NGS/PCR)
picks.rationale: A confirmed BRAF V600E gives a doublet that NCCN BTC v2.2025 (category 2A, subsequent-line) and the tumor-agnostic FDA label both endorse, with the ROAR biliary cohort at ORR 47% (95% CI 31-62) and median PFS 9.0 months. The cross-society and cross-label convergence is real, but I hold it at rank 5 because V600E turns up in only about 1-5% of BTC and the cohort is small (n=43) and single-arm. The gate is a true V600E on NGS or PCR; a VE1 IHC screen alone, or a class 2/3 BRAF alteration, does not qualify. Pyrexia is the signature combination effect and comes with a standard dose-hold and antipyretic playbook the consensus assumes is in place.
primary_concerns: BRAF V600E is untested (ngs_pending); only a confirmed V600E on NGS/PCR meets the gate, IHC alone and class 2/3 alterations do not.
Category 2A here rests on a small single-arm basket cohort (n=43).
Pyrexia drove the treatment-related serious AEs at 21% and needs the monitoring the guideline presumes, unconfirmed against absent baseline data.

notes: Re-run over the full current option set (16 new on-axis trials plus their evidence). Scope-unknown CCA, every candidate feature ngs_pending, so comprehensive genomic profiling stays the rank-1 gating workup and all five picks are conditional on a positive confirmatory test (RNA fusion panel, DNA NGS over IDH1/BRAF/KRAS hotspots, HER2 IHC with reflex ISH, MMR/MSI). I rank on guideline endorsement and cross-society convergence, not raw effect size. One thing changed since the last run: NCCN BTC v2.2025 now grades ivosidenib category 1 for IDH1-mutant subsequent-line disease (my prior pass had it 2A), so it is the only category-1 anchor in the set and keeps rank 1, with the 2024 ESMO interim update recommending it (MCBS 2). The FGFR2 pair follows, futibatinib ahead of pemigatinib on the kinase-domain resistance sequencing edge rather than any MCBS difference; ESMO scores the FGFR-inhibitor class at MCBS 3 as a class, so I dropped the earlier futibatinib-over-pemigatinib MCBS claim as over-precise. Zanidatamab is the HER2 lead (NCCN 2A, dedicated biliary trial) over basket-route T-DXd, and dab+tram rounds out the five on NCCN 2A plus the tumor-agnostic label. Off the ranked five but guideline-endorsed if their feature reads positive: pembrolizumab (MSI-H/dMMR and TMB-high, tumor-agnostic labels, though KEYNOTE-158 reports no CCA-specific subgroup ORR), larotrectinib/entrectinib (NTRK, tumor-agnostic), selpercatinib (RET, tumor-agnostic). The 16 new agents do not change the guideline-anchored top five: lirafugratinib (FGFR2-selective, ReFocus ORR 46.5%) is under FDA priority review with a 27 Sept 2026 PDUFA date but is not yet approved or NCCN-listed, so it belongs in the trial-enrollment lane, not the ranked set; tinengotinib (phase 3), gunagratinib, fanregratinib (China NMPA priority review), 3D185, olutasidenib (approved in IDH1 AML, off-label in solid tumors), and zurletrectinib are all investigational or non-Western-registered on this axis and off-guideline for CCA. Adagrasib for KRAS G12C stays off the five: the biliary readout is a 12-patient cohort (ROBINS-I Serious) and no society lists a BTC-specific KRAS G12C recommendation, so trial enrollment is the guideline-aligned route there. Every NCCN category cited is verbatim from v2.2025; note that only ivosidenib reaches category 1 in BTC, and the rest are 2A because the consensus has calibrated the same single-arm and surrogate-driven evidence the critic reads and landed there. If real molecular results, prior lines, performance status, or organ-function labs arrive, re-run intake; the ranking narrows to whichever feature reads positive.

picks.intervention_label: Comprehensive genomic profiling (paired DNA + RNA fusion NGS with MSI/TMB) plus HER2 IHC with reflex ISH and MMR IHC
picks.rationale: Nothing else on this list can be chosen until this is done. The patient has eight candidate targets and zero results, so the single action that actually helps them is the test that tells us which axis is real. A paired DNA + RNA panel resolves seven of the eight features in one pass, and the RNA arm matters because DNA-only calling misses FGFR2 fusions with odd breakpoints, the exact axis with the best odds here. I pair it with HER2 IHC and reflex ISH because the approved HER2 drugs key off protein and ISH, not an NGS amplification number, and with MMR IHC because a checkpoint-eligible dMMR case is rare but changes everything if it turns up. Roughly two in five of these patients carry an actionable alteration; skipping the workup leaves that on the table and leaves the patient on chemo alone. It reads on archival tissue in 2 to 3 weeks, or ctDNA in about a week if tissue is short, and it costs the patient nothing in toxicity. On the preferences: efficacy/toxicity weight sits at a balanced 0.5, no vetoes, no modality constraints, and the user wants trials surfaced, all of which this step serves without tension since it is the gate for every downstream option, on-label or investigational.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: no toxicity veto to clear, no modality constraint, and this is the enabling step for the trials the user asked to see first.
Archival tissue may be exhausted or too old for reliable RNA; a ctDNA parallel draw is the fallback but reads fusions less sensitively.
In tension only with time: a 2-to-3-week turnaround delays any therapy start, so first-line chemotherapy decisions cannot wait indefinitely on the result.

picks.intervention_label: Lirafugratinib (RLY-4008), FGFR2-selective, via the ReFocus cohort (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: FGFR2 fusion is the axis most likely to test positive at 10 to 15% of intrahepatic disease, and among the FGFR options this is the one whose design fits a balanced efficacy/toxicity preference best. Because it is FGFR2-selective it largely spares the FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia that dogs pemigatinib and futibatinib, where hyperphosphatemia runs 30 to 55%; the ReFocus cohort instead reports ORR 46.5% (95% CI 37.1-56.1), median PFS 11.3 months, and a 96.5% disease-control rate, with the main grade 3+ events being hand-foot skin reaction and stomatitis. That is a cleaner tolerability trade at a response rate matching or beating the approved agents, which is exactly what a 0.5 weight should favor. It is oral and, since the user wants trials surfaced first, it is enrollable now through ReFocus with an NDA under FDA priority review. The honest caveat is that this is abstract-stage data with no PMID yet, so if the patient needs an established on-label option today, pemigatinib or futibatinib is the ranked-3 fallback on the same axis.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: oral, best tolerability profile on the FGFR axis for a balanced weight, and enrollable now which serves the trials-first preference.
In tension with evidence maturity: ReFocus is a single-arm phase 1/2 cohort reported in abstract with no peer-reviewed PMID yet, so certainty is lower than for the approved FGFR agents.
FGFR2 status is untested; a negative fusion read closes this axis entirely.

picks.intervention_label: Futibatinib (FDA-approved, on-label; if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
picks.rationale: This is the established, on-label safety net for the same FGFR2 axis, and I rank it right behind the selective agent so the patient is never stuck choosing between the best-tolerated option and a proven one. FOENIX-CCA2 showed ORR 42% (95% CI 32-52), median PFS 9.0 months, median OS 21.7 months, and only 2% discontinued for toxicity, which is a strong durability record. The irreversible binding also holds against several kinase-domain mutations that defeat pemigatinib, so it buys a second FGFR move if the patient progresses. The cost is the on-target hyperphosphatemia, grade 3+ in 30%, which needs active phosphate management but is manageable and not a stated veto. Oral, once daily. Between the two approved FGFR agents I put futibatinib ahead of pemigatinib on the slightly higher response rate and the lower discontinuation rate.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: FDA-approved on-label oral option, no veto to clear, balanced tolerability that a 0.5 weight accepts.
Hyperphosphatemia is near-universal on target and grade 3+ in 30%, so it needs phosphate monitoring even though no toxicity veto was set.
Approval and trial eligibility were built on intrahepatic CCA, so a non-intrahepatic subsite weakens the match, and the fusion is untested.

picks.intervention_label: Ivosidenib (FDA-approved, on-label; if IDH1 R132 confirmed)
picks.rationale: IDH1 R132 is the second most likely axis to land at 15 to 20% of intrahepatic disease, and this is the only randomized phase 3 in the whole dossier, ClarIDHy, with a PFS hazard ratio of 0.37 (p<0.0001). For a patient who values evidence quality, that randomized read is worth a lot. It is also the gentlest option here: grade 3+ events tracked placebo, ascites was the most common at 7%, and there were no treatment-related deaths, so on the tolerability side of a balanced weight it is easy to defend. What holds it at rank 4 rather than higher is the modest single-agent payoff, median PFS 2.7 versus 1.4 months and ORR only 2%, so the realistic goal is holding disease steady rather than shrinking it. Oral, once daily. If the patient wants more than stabilization, the preclinical work pointing to an immune-mediated mechanism and synergy with CTLA-4 blockade is the reason to ask about an ivosidenib-plus-checkpoint trial, which also serves the trials-first preference.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: cleanest safety profile in the set, oral, on-label, and the only randomized evidence, which suits a patient weighting evidence and tolerability evenly.
Absolute single-agent benefit is small (median PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 months; ORR 2%) despite the strong hazard ratio, so expectations need framing.
IDH1 hotspot is untested, and the OS read was blunted by 70% placebo-to-ivosidenib crossover.

picks.intervention_label: Zanidatamab (FDA-approved, on-label; if HER2 IHC-positive with reflex ISH confirmed)
picks.rationale: If HER2 tests positive this is the option I would put in front of the patient first, and I rank it above T-DXd deliberately on the user's behalf. HERIZON-BTC-01 gave a confirmed ORR 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8) with median DoR 12.9 months, and the safety read is favorable: the main concern is a 3% grade 3 ejection-fraction drop that baseline and serial cardiac monitoring handles. Trastuzumab deruxtecan carries adjudicated interstitial lung disease at 10.5% with three treatment-related deaths in DESTINY-PanTumor02, and while no toxicity veto was stated, a balanced 0.5 weight should not reach for the ILD-risk ADC when a comparably effective antibody with a milder profile is available on the same axis. HER2 skews toward extrahepatic and gallbladder disease and the subsite is unknown here, which is the real uncertainty. The gate is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH, not the DNA copy-number call alone, so the rank-1 workup has to include the protein readout. If the patient specifically wants a trial, several HER2-positive BTC cohorts are recruiting, which serves the trials-first preference.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: on-label, and the milder cardiac profile beats the T-DXd ILD signal on the user's behalf under a balanced weight, even with no explicit veto set.
Gated on HER2 IHC plus reflex ISH, not NGS alone; HER2 prevalence depends on a subsite that is unspecified at intake.
Decreased ejection fraction is a HER2-directed class effect and no baseline cardiac function was supplied, so monitoring is required.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab (FDA-approved, on-label; if MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high confirmed)
picks.rationale: This is the low-prevalence, high-payoff pick I keep on the ranked list because when it lands it is durable in a way nothing else here is. MSI-H/dMMR runs only 1 to 3% in biliary cancer, but KEYNOTE-158 showed ORR 34.3% with median OS 23.5 months in the MSI-H basket, and the TMB-high subgroup reached ORR 29% with responses still ongoing past two years. The same rank-1 panel returns both the MSI call and the TMB number, and MMR IHC is a cheap orthogonal check that catches cases a low-purity NGS score can miss, so there is no extra burden to chase it. Grade 3+ treatment-related events sat at 14.6%, lower than most targeted options here, which fits a balanced weight. The reason it is sixth and not higher is prevalence alone; on effect-per-positive-test it earns its place, and the durability is the argument to run the MMR IHC alongside the DNA panel rather than waiting.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: lowest grade 3+ rate among the targeted options, on-label, and resolved by the same rank-1 workup at no added cost.
Prevalence is the constraint at 1-3% MSI-H, so the test is most often negative; no CCA-specific subgroup ORR was published in KEYNOTE-158.
Immune-mediated toxicity is the characteristic checkpoint risk; no veto was set, but it warrants counseling.

notes: Scope-unknown CCA, all eight candidate features ngs_pending, so I read the preference file as a set of neutral defaults rather than active constraints: efficacy/toxicity weight 0.5 (balanced), no toxicity vetoes, no modality constraints, prefers_trials true. That last one is the only preference with teeth here, and it points the same direction as the clinical logic, so there is no conflict to flag. I foreground the comprehensive workup at rank 1 because it is the one action that actually helps a patient with zero results, and I ranked the therapeutic picks by expected value to the user: FGFR2-selective lirafugratinib ahead of the approved FGFR agents on tolerability at equal response, then IDH1 for its randomized evidence, then HER2 with zanidatamab placed above T-DXd on the user's behalf given the ILD signal even though no veto was stated, then pembrolizumab for durability despite low prevalence. I did NOT invent preferences the file does not state: the tolerability tie-breaks (selective FGFR over pan-FGFR, zanidatamab over T-DXd) are justified under the balanced 0.5 weight, not under a veto the patient never set. NTRK/RET/KRAS G12C and pemigatinib all remain defensible if their feature tests positive and the same panel resolves them; they sit just below the ranked six on effect-times-prevalence. Every pick re-ranks the moment real molecular results, prior lines, or actual patient preferences land.
